surface_mechanism_description: Different surface phases of Al or Al(CH3)n (n = 1, 2) exist on the As-terminated AlAs surface. When Al atoms (or methylaluminum molecules) on the growing surface form a two-dimensional layer with a surface density of 2 monolayers, the surface is defined as a 2D(2ML)-phase surface. This phase may deposit Al atoms with a self-limiting process (2 ML/cycle). The 3D phase is defined as the growing surface where Al atoms form a cluster-like three-dimensional phase. The existence of two- and three-dimensional phases was also suggested from the fact that Al atoms of the 2D(2ML) Al phase react with ASH3 for a very short time (< 1 s) in ASH3 dependence experiments, while 3D Al phase reacts longer.
